To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the jute fibers are successfully converted to the nanofibrillated cellulose and the nanocomposites are successfully prepared by using the nanocelluloses.
the jute fiber waste can be used to produce the cellulose nanofibers by using the chemical treatment with ionic liquid and subsequent acid hydrolysis.
we have prepared nanocelluloses from jute fiber wastes and studied its effect on the mechanical properties of polyvinyl alcohol.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel method for isolation of nanofibrils from the short waste fibers of jute and their characterization using different techniques such as scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
the preparation of nanocrystals from waste jute fibers.
the isolation of nanocellulosic materials (NCM) from jute fiber and its use as the fillers to prepare the jute fiber based nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanocelluloses from natural fibers can be prepared from the waste fibers by using various techniques and can be utilized in the preparation of nanocomposite materials.
the short natural fibers can be used for production of nanofibers and nanocrystals which can further be used for preparation of nanocomposite materials with improved properties.

the short fibers have been used as a raw material for the preparation of cellulose nanofibers.7−11 The cellulose nanofiber (CNF) is a promising candidate as a reinforcing filler in the preparation of nanocomposite due to its high strength and modulus, high specific surface area and low density.12−14 However, it is not possible to obtain CNF from the natural fibers in a single step.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to prepare nanocelluloses, we used steam explosion method to extract the cellulose from jute fibers.
, the jute fiber waste was treated with 2% NaOH solution at 80 °C for 30 min to obtain a homogenous dispersion of the nanocelluloses.

the nanocelluloses were isolated from the waste jute fibers and the effect of the isolated nanocellulosis on the physical and mechanical properties of polypropylene (PP) and high density polyethylene (HDPE) nanocomposites was studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jute fiber waste, if properly treated, can be a potential source for the isolation of cellulose nanocrystals.
we can use the waste fibers as the source to prepare nanocelluloses.
we have successfully isolated the cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) from the waste jute fibers by using steam explosion method and used it to prepare cellulose nanocomposites.
